scope: Fresh isolated Chrome profiles, localhost HTTP test server with Cache-Control no-store, frozen 512-match tournament response. All server calls and export markers simulated. No player data included.
changes: Remove the eager Excel and PDF vendor scripts from the entry page. A shared loader requests each dependency on first use and reuses existing globals and concurrent requests.

Certificate XLSX export waits for Excel before generating the file or sending an export marker. Loading, error, retry and disposal keep the existing input locking and prevent late output after disposal.
Accounting invoices, receipts and position-list PDFs await the shared PDF loader. Certificate rendering shares the same PDF request while retaining its existing font loading.
Only invalidate initial navigation font metrics through fonts.ready if fonts are actually still loading. Later loadingdone events and ResizeObserver remain subscribed.

comparison.order: before, after, after, before; no CPU profiler
comparison.meaning: File/script phase is DOMContentLoaded. Build phase begins after fixture preparation and ends after three frames without pending UI work. The navigation-to-ready metric additionally includes test-snapshot injection and fixture overhead; it is not a real production reload latency.

test_maintenance: The existing certificate navigation assertion now includes the already-present Buchhaltung tab and still strictly checks the full navigation.
The XLSX workflow waits for asynchronous dependency loading before asserting the real file contents. No file or output assertions were removed.
limitations: Two runs per variant; local uncached startup. Warm-cache and slower-network gains can differ.
The first requested export now loads its dependency; subsequent exports reuse it.
No meaningful browser-build latency reduction is established by these samples (1019 vs 1011 ms). The remaining approximately one-second UI build is a separate bottleneck.
No backend, database, BTP write path, file format or BUP client changes.
